ZELTGOLD · 0→1 PRODUCT DESIGN

Not one app,an entire product.

Zeltgold is a gold-savings platform: buy real, jewellery-grade gold from ₹100 a month. Its website, customer app, vendor app, admin console and redemption desk were researched, designed and shipped to production. Solo, in a month.

RESEARCH THROUGH UI
The challenge

Zeltgold had a working gold-savings engine and no product around it. Buying gold in India is a high-trust, intimidating decision, and the jewellers who run instalment schemes still track them on paper. It had to earn a jeweller's trust and a first-time saver's confidence at once, on every surface.

The solution

One design system that stretches from the first screen a saver sees to the daily counter workflow. The customer app turns buying gold into a ₹100 habit; the vendor app and admin treat that balance as gold owed; a redemption desk verifies before it hands over metal, all speaking one visual language and one shared ledger.

Scope

It spans research to product, but it isn't five separate projects. It's one visual language stretched from the first screen a customer sees to the ledger a jeweller settles, so the trust story stays legible at every step.

01 · WHY IT'S BIGGER THAN AN APP

The app is the part people see. It's a quarter of the work.

5surfaces
2roles, saver & jeweller
1shared ledger

Everyone downloads the customer app. Behind it, three more systems do the real work: the vendor app that collects instalments, the admin console that tracks every rupee owed, and the redemption desk that hands over real gold. Get one number wrong across them and someone loses money. That's the part I had to get right.

From the customer's tap to the platform's ledger, the same transaction stays true across every surface.

07

A month alone taught me where the real complexity hides.

looking back
i.

Simplify the plan language.

Before adding another screen to explain a scheme, I cut the words the first one didn't need.

ii.

Lead with what's owed, not what's grown.

Vendors trusted the ledger more once "you owe" outranked "you've earned."

iii.

Fewer steps, stronger checks.

Verification at redemption should feel like one motion, not an interrogation.
